question: What architecture is the famous black pagoda temple situated in Konark?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalinga architecture.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Konark Sun Temple (Konark Surya Mandir) is a 13th-century CE Sun Temple at Konark about 35 kilometers northeast from Puri on the coastline of Odisha, India.
 
• It is a classic illustration of the Odisha style of Architecture or Kalinga Architecture. Hence, the correct answer is option 3.
 
• The temple is attributed to king Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty about 1250 CE.
 
• Dedicated to the Hindu Sun God Surya, what remains of the temple complex has the appearance of a 100-foot (30 m) high chariot with immense wheels and horses, all carved from stone. 
 
• This temple was called the "Black Pagoda" in European sailor accounts as early as 1676 because it looked like a great tower that appeared black.
 
• Declared a UNESCO world heritage site in 1984, it remains a major pilgrimage site for Hindus, who gather here every year for the Chandrabhaga Mela around the month of February.
 
• Konark Sun Temple is depicted on the reverse side of the Indian currency note of Rs 10 to signify its importance to Indian cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42e6ef434dfd64511a86113467b5bc57ce6ed8185cd26dcab20dedf4d5a7b8e7.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Dravidian Architecture:**

 
• The Pallavas established the Dravidian style of temple architecture in South India.
 
• Up to the ninth century, the Pallavas ruled over areas of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and northern Tamil Nadu.
 
• The key features of this type of temple construction are:
 
 
• A compound wall encloses the Dravida temple.
 
• A Gopuram, or entrance doorway, is located in the middle of the front wall.
 
• The shape of the main temple tower known as vimana, is like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically rather than the curving shikhara of North India.
 
• The word "shikhara" is only used in reference to the temple's top element, which is typically fashioned like a miniature stupika or an octagonal cupola.
 
• The entrance to the garbhagriha is adorned with fierce Dvarapalas, or the doorkeepers, guarding the temple.
 
• A sizable water tank, sometimes known as a temple tank, is frequently found encased within the complex.
 
• Subsidiary shrines are either incorporated within the main temple tower, or located as distinct, separate small shrines beside the main temple.
